Is a hybrid animal evolution's next upgrade — or a gorgeous genetic dead-end?

Some hybrids are ancient and everywhere, like the mule. Some fall apart, like the leopon. Some are wild accidents nobody saw coming — like the pizzly, a wild-born polar-grizzly cross first spotted in the Canadian Arctic in 2006. And a few, like the Clymene dolphin and the Big Bird finch of the Galápagos, didn't just blur two species — they became brand-new ones.

So we tracked down the 20 most significant hybrids on the planet: the ligers and the mules, the ones that thrive like the killer bee, the ones that fall apart like the leopon, and the real reason each one exists — from the breeding pen to the open ocean to a melting Arctic where species that wer
title: These Hybrids Shouldn't Exist
